To decouple the Conversation Engine, Context Engine, and Application Orchestrator, you can create separate components for each role. Here's a high-level overview of how you can structure these components:

1. **Conversation Engine**:
   - **Message Storage**: This component stores all messages in a database or a file system. It provides a way to retrieve and manage messages.
   - **Message Processing**: This component processes incoming messages and generates responses. It can interact with other components to get information about the conversation context.
   - **Message Routing**: This component decides which message to process next based on the conversation state and user input.

2. **Context Engine**:
   - **Reference Selection**: This component selects the appropriate references based on the context of the conversation. It can interact with other components to get information about the conversation state and user input.
   - **Reference Budgeting**: This component budgets the references based on the available budget. It can interact with other components to get information about the conversation state and user input.

3. **Application Orchestrator**:
   - **Message Dispatch**: This component dispatches messages to the appropriate components based on the conversation state and user input. It can interact with other components to get information about the conversation state and user input.
   - **Context Update**: This component updates the context based on the responses from the Conversation Engine. It can interact with other components to get information about the conversation state and user input.

By decoupling these components, you can make each component more independent and easier to maintain and scale. This separation of concerns also makes it easier to integrate new components or modify existing ones without affecting the other components.

For UI an optional second line STATE followed by one space and a JSON object of initial integer inputs is allowed. No fences. No JavaScript, tools, events, HTML or links. One Stack with unique named leaves. Up to 40 leaves, 40 collection members, 64 declarations, depth 32, 16000 UTF-8 source bytes, 10000 frame bytes. Integers for input state. Names start with ASCII letter, then alphanumeric or underscore, at most 48 characters. All declarations must be reachable. Text and labels at most 512 characters. Safe Graphic items use kind plus only required fields: rect(x,y,width,height), circle(cx,cy,r), text(x,y,text), path(d using only M L H V Z, lowercase equivalents, numbers, spaces or commas), group(items of leaves). Numeric coordinates 0..640; viewBox 0 0 450 135.
Return strict JSON with only root (element ID) and elements (object). Root element {"type":"Stack","props":{},"children":["leafId"]}. Each leaf has only type and props. Text props {text}; Metric {label,value}; Control {label,min,max,choices,value:{"$bindState":"/name"}}; Table {values:[{label,score}]}; Graphic {label,items}. Numeric inputs default to minima unless STATE supplies every binding. Read with {"$state":"/name"}. Computations use {"$computed":"Add","args":{"a":number,"b":number}}; Multiply and Excess have the same args, Excess means max(0,a-b). Rank takes args rows (array of [name,[three numeric scores]]), a,b,c (numeric weights) and produces sorted weighted rows. No other functions, properties or nesting of components.
